solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Follow fellow getting drunk, losing head in melee

parts.note: to dog someone is to follow them closely

indicators.note: the drunk word must drop its first letter, its head

parts.note: tight is informal for drunk

explanation.surface: A man gets drunk and is pursued through a brawl, losing his head in the chaos.
explanation.walkthrough: 'losing head' cuts the T from TIGHT, leaving IGHT.
explanation.definitionFit: A dogfight is a confused close-quarters scrap, so a synonym for a chaotic brawl.

clue.text: Turkey I had raised with German around start of week

indicators.note: in a down clue raised means the contraction is read upwards, backwards

parts.note: I had contracts to I'd, written ID

indicators.note: the German word goes around the chosen letter

parts.note: mit is German for with, so 'with German' gives the German word

indicators.note: only the opening letter of week is taken

explanation.surface: Someone describes raising a turkey with a German friend over the weekend.
explanation.walkthrough: 'with German' is MIT, the German word for 'with'; 'raised' turns ID into DI.
explanation.definitionFit: Turkey is slang, chiefly American, for a stupid or useless person, a fool.

clue.text: Spirit displayed by girl following dope

indicators.note: following puts the girl's name after the word for dope

parts.note: gen is British slang for information, as is dope
Eva is a girl's name

explanation.surface: A girl shows spirit after taking drugs.
explanation.walkthrough: GEN is British slang for inside information, which is what dope also means.
explanation.definitionFit: Geneva is an old name for gin, a Dutch-style juniper spirit, so an example of a spirit.

clue.text: Very unpleasant line ran surprisingly about force

indicators.note: the rearranged letters sit about, around, the letter for force
surprisingly signals that the letters of line and ran turn up in an unexpected order

parts.note: F is the abbreviation for force in physics

explanation.surface: A railway line surprisingly ran into a nasty force.
explanation.walkthrough: 'line' and 'ran' look like a railway story, but they are only letters for 'surprisingly' to reshuffle.
explanation.definitionFit: Infernal, literally hellish, is used informally to mean dreadful or detestable.

clue.text: Entertainer sought-after around society

indicators.note: the word for sought-after goes around the society letter

parts.note: a hot item is one everyone wants

explanation.surface: A popular entertainer is much in demand on the social scene.
explanation.definitionFit: A host entertains guests, so the person entertaining is a synonym.

clue.text: Justice with stable employee almost getting push?

parts.note: J is the abbreviation for Justice, as in a judge's title

indicators.note: almost means the stable worker loses its final letter

parts.note: an ostler looks after horses at an inn's stable

explanation.surface: A judge and a groom nearly come to blows in a shoving match.
explanation.definitionFit: To jostle is to push and shove roughly, so a synonym; the question mark marks the verb doing duty for a noun-like push.

clue.text: Museum with head leaving imports European work

indicators.note: the shortened museum takes the European letter into itself
the museum's name drops its first letter, its head

parts.note: the Louvre is the great Paris art museum

explanation.surface: A museum whose director has left brings in a European masterpiece.
explanation.walkthrough: 'with head leaving' trims LOUVRE to OUVRE; 'imports' takes E in after the O.
explanation.definitionFit: Oeuvre is the French word for a work, or an artist's whole body of work.

clue.text: Remove a burger?

definitions.meaning: a burger bought from a shop and eaten elsewhere is a ... meal; the question mark flags it as an example

explanation.surface: Someone asks to have a burger taken off the table.
explanation.definitionFit: Take away means remove, and a takeaway is ready-cooked food bought to eat off the premises, such as a burger.

clue.text: Classical character in international grouping with theatrical effect departs a bit later?

parts.note: EU is the European Union

indicators.note: the departs letter is moved a bit further along in the word for the stage effect

parts.note: dry ice makes stage fog
D is the abbreviation for departs on timetables

explanation.surface: A classical figure appears through stage fog on an international tour and leaves late.
explanation.walkthrough: 'a bit later' shifts the D of DRYICE two places on, giving RYDICE.
explanation.definitionFit: Eurydice is the wife of Orpheus in Greek myth, a figure of classical legend.

clue.text: Show incomplete set of proposals

indicators.note: incomplete means the word for the proposals loses its last letter

parts.note: a party manifesto sets out its proposed policies

explanation.surface: A party presents only part of its policy programme.
explanation.definitionFit: To manifest something is to display or reveal it, a synonym for show.

clue.text: Duck to avoid college friend

indicators.note: the duck word must avoid, do without, the college letter

parts.note: a quacker is a whimsical name for a duck

explanation.surface: Someone ducks out of college to avoid a friend.
explanation.walkthrough: Lower-case 'friend' hides the capital: members of the Religious Society of Friends are called Friends.
explanation.definitionFit: Quakers belong to the Religious Society of Friends, so each one is called a Friend.

clue.text: Cultivate concession in Midlands town

parts.note: to work the land is to cultivate it
a sop is something given to placate, a concession

explanation.surface: A farmer is granted land to cultivate near a Midlands town.
explanation.walkthrough: The Midlands is the central region of England.
explanation.definitionFit: Worksop is a market town in Nottinghamshire in the English East Midlands.

clue.text: Turn favoured by thriller? I go to hide!

parts.note: to be in with someone is to be favoured

indicators.note: the letters of the phrase go into hiding, taken out of the film title

parts.note: Vertigo is Hitchcock's 1958 thriller
taken as written, the letters I, G, O

explanation.surface: A favoured line from a thriller: someone announces they will go and hide.
explanation.walkthrough: 'I go to hide' removes IGO from VERTIGO, leaving VERT.
explanation.definitionFit: To invert is to turn something upside down, a synonym for turn.

clue.text: Low light around river, a feature of Yorkshire?

indicators.note: the two words together sit around the river letter

parts.note: to low is to moo, as cattle do
to light is to land, as a bird lights on a branch

explanation.surface: Low light hangs over a river in a Yorkshire landscape.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Low' and 'light' are verbs, not the dim glow they seem.
explanation.definitionFit: Yorkshire is famous for its wild upland heath, the North York Moors, so an example of its scenery.

clue.text: Give rough figure for drinks being promoted

parts.note: a round is a set of drinks bought for a group
someone promoted is moving up

explanation.surface: An estimate of the drinks bill after someone's promotion.
explanation.definitionFit: To round up a number is to take it to the next whole value, an approximation.

clue.text: Graduate holding instrument with introduction delayed? It might be seen in action

definitions.text: It might be seen in action

indicators.note: the graduate letters hold the altered instrument between them

parts.note: BA, Bachelor of Arts, is a graduate

indicators.note: the instrument's first letter, its introduction, is moved to the end

parts.note: a kazoo is a toy instrument you hum into

explanation.surface: A graduate musician turns up late with an instrument, a scene from a performance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'with introduction delayed' moves K from the front of KAZOO to the back, AZOOK.
explanation.definitionFit: A bazooka is an anti-tank rocket launcher, a weapon seen in military action.

clue.text: Powdery stuff, stash of fatal cocaine

indicators.note: the answer is stashed away inside the letters of the words that follow

explanation.surface: A deadly stash of cocaine, the kind of white powder police seize.
explanation.definitionFit: Talc is a soft mineral ground into a fine powder for skin care.

clue.text: Two Cabinet ministers defending line? It might be part of plot

definitions.text: It might be part of plot

parts.note: Liam Fox, a Conservative Cabinet minister

indicators.note: the second minister surrounds and so defends the line letter

parts.note: Michael Gove, another Conservative Cabinet minister

explanation.surface: Two Cabinet ministers hold the line amid what may be a political plot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'plot' is a garden plot, not a conspiracy. Fox and Gove were both Conservative Cabinet ministers.
explanation.definitionFit: The foxglove is a tall flowering plant common in British gardens, so it may grow in a plot.

clue.text: Meat with care cooked — tourist fare?

indicators.note: cooked signals that the letters of meat and care are prepared into a new form

explanation.surface: A dish of meat cooked carefully, served to visitors.
explanation.walkthrough: A cream tea is scones with clotted cream and jam served with tea, a British teashop treat.
explanation.definitionFit: This scones-and-cream afternoon spread is a classic treat offered to visitors in Devon and Cornwall.

clue.text: Convince uppity businessman to take action about bill

indicators.note: in a down clue uppity has the businessman read upwards, backwards

parts.note: a rep is a sales representative

indicators.note: the legal word goes about the bill word

parts.note: to sue is to take legal action
an ad, advertisement, is a bill or poster

explanation.surface: An arrogant businessman is persuaded to sue over an unpaid bill.
explanation.walkthrough: 'uppity' works because this is a down clue, where reversed letters read upwards.
explanation.definitionFit: To persuade someone is to talk them into belief or action, a synonym for convince.

clue.text: Horrific party putting government in tangle

indicators.note: the government letter is put in the seaweed word

parts.note: tangle and ore (as in oreweed) are both seaweeds

explanation.surface: A dreadful political party leaves the government in a mess.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tangle' looks like a mess but is a seaweed; ORE is an old name for seaweed. 'party' means a person.
explanation.definitionFit: An ogre is a monstrous or cruel person, and party can mean a person, so a horrible individual.

clue.text: An activity supplying pots?

parts.note: sounds like pottery, but pots here are shots that sink balls in a cue game

explanation.surface: A craft that produces pottery.
explanation.walkthrough: British players of this cue sport call sinking a ball a pot.
explanation.definitionFit: Snooker is a cue game in which players score by potting balls.

clue.text: Conservative follows with no end of intrigue count

indicators.note: no means the word for follows goes without the chosen letter

parts.note: ensues means follows on

indicators.note: only the last letter of intrigue is taken

explanation.surface: A Conservative follows up on a plot to rig a count.
explanation.walkthrough: 'no end of intrigue' drops E from ENSUES, leaving ENSUS.
explanation.definitionFit: A census is an official count of a population.

clue.text: Footballer in the same place in new role

indicators.note: the reference abbreviation is set in the rearranged letters
new signals that the letters of role take a new arrangement

parts.note: ib, short for ibidem, means in the same place in references

explanation.surface: A footballer stays in the same club but in a new position.
explanation.walkthrough: IB is short for ibidem, used in footnotes for 'in the same place'; a libero is a sweeper.
explanation.definitionFit: A libero is a sweeper, a defender who plays free behind the back line in football.

clue.text: Eastern couple of islands still largely restricting mass set of proteins

parts.note: NZ, New Zealand, is chiefly two islands, North and South

indicators.note: the shortened word for still restricts, holds in, the mass letter
largely means most of the word for still, without its last letter

parts.note: yet can mean still, as in 'yet more'

explanation.surface: In the east, two islands still largely limit a mass of proteins.
explanation.walkthrough: 'largely' cuts YET to YE; 'restricting' puts M inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: An enzyme is a protein that speeds a chemical reaction, a class of proteins rather than a single one.

clue.text: Old cricketer to roll up right away having attractive quality

parts.note: W G Grace was the great Victorian cricketer

indicators.note: away means the right letter is taken out of the word for roll up

parts.note: to furl a flag or sail is to roll it up

explanation.surface: A veteran cricketer rolls up his sleeves elegantly.
explanation.walkthrough: W G Grace was England's most famous cricketer of the Victorian era.
explanation.definitionFit: Graceful describes elegant, pleasing movement or form, so having an attractive quality.

clue.text: Put forward a function for audience

indicators.note: for audience means what is heard by listeners, not what is written

parts.note: a sine is a trigonometric function, so 'a function' gives a sine

explanation.surface: Someone proposes a role for the people watching.
explanation.definitionFit: To assign a task or person is to allot or designate them, to put them forward for something.

clue.text: Excite bird

definitions.meaning: to ... up feelings is to excite them
bird, from bird-lime, rhyming slang for time, is British slang for a prison sentence; slang for prison

explanation.definitionFit: Stir means to rouse or agitate, and both stir and bird are British slang for prison or a spell inside.

clue.text: Foolish group of workers, section interrupting award

indicators.note: the union and section letters break into the middle of the award

parts.note: the OBE is the British honour Officer of the Order of the British Empire
TU is a trade union, a body of workers

explanation.surface: A foolish union faction disrupts an awards ceremony.
explanation.walkthrough: The OBE is a British honour awarded by the monarch.
explanation.definitionFit: Obtuse means slow to understand, dim-witted, a synonym for foolish.

clue.text: Finesse shown by dog perhaps rounding sheep

indicators.note: the stray word goes round the sheep word, as a sheepdog rounds up a flock

parts.note: a stray is a homeless animal, a dog for example
a teg is a sheep in its second year

explanation.surface: A sheepdog shows skill in rounding up the flock.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dog perhaps' is not a sheepdog but STRAY; TEG is a two-year-old sheep.
explanation.definitionFit: Finesse can mean clever handling or tactics, close to a skilful plan.

clue.text: Pass first of exams associated with liberal part of church

indicators.note: only the opening letter of exams is taken

parts.note: the apse is the rounded end of a church beyond the altar

explanation.surface: A student passes the first exams in a liberal church school.
explanation.definitionFit: Time is said to elapse when it passes or goes by.

clue.text: Such might be morgues at work with the ultimate in gore?

definitions.text: Such might be morgues at work with the ultimate in gore?

indicators.note: at work signals that the letters of morgues and the extra letter get worked into a new order
only the final letter of gore is taken

explanation.surface: Mortuaries busy with bloody remains are a grim sight.
explanation.walkthrough: 'at work' rearranges MORGUES with E, the last letter of 'gore'; the whole clue then describes the result.
explanation.definitionFit: Busy mortuaries full of blood are horrible places, so the whole clue paints something ghastly.
